questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Cartesian Function With Respect to Plane Polar Coordinates
questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=2xy+{y}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂f}{∂\theta },$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $f(x,y)$ with two independent variables $r$ and $\theta ,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂\theta } & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂\theta }+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂\theta } \\  & =-\frac{∂f}{∂x}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{∂f}{∂y}r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r$ and $\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta , \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂\theta } & =-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +(2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ) \\  & =2{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )+{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Polar Function With Respect to Cartesian Coordinates
questions.problem: Given that $u(r,\theta )=r\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta ,$ find $\frac{∂u}{∂y},$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
questions.worked_solution:
We will make use of the following chain rule formula:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂y}=\frac{∂u}{∂r}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{r}\frac{∂u}{∂\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $u$ with respect to $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂r}=\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta ,\,\frac{∂u}{∂\theta }=4r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Then, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{r}(4r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta +4\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Polar Function With Respect to Cartesian Coordinates
questions.problem: Given that $u(r,\theta )=r(2+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ),$ find $\frac{∂u}{∂x},$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
questions.worked_solution:
We will make use of the following chain rule formula:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=\frac{∂u}{∂r}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\frac{1}{r}\frac{∂u}{∂\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $u$ with respect to $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂r}=2+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\frac{∂u}{∂\theta }=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Then, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =(2+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\frac{1}{r}(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Cartesian Function With Respect to Cylindrical Polar Coordinates
questions.problem: Given that $g(x,y,z)={x}^{3}{z}^{4}+{y}^{3}{z}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂g}{∂r},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $g(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂r} & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂r}+\frac{∂g}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂r}+\frac{∂g}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂r} \\  & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{∂g}{∂y}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $g$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x}=3{x}^{2}{z}^{4},\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =3{r}^{2}{z}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta , \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =3{r}^{2}{z}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂r} & =(3{r}^{2}{z}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +(3{r}^{2}{z}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =3{r}^{2}{z}^{2}({z}^{2}{cos}^{3}⁡\theta +{sin}^{3}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Cartesian Function With Respect to Cylindrical Polar Coordinates
questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)={y}^{2}{z}^{2}+xz,$ find $\frac{∂f}{∂z},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $f(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂z}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂z}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂f}{∂z}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂z}=2{y}^{2}z+x\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂z} & =2{r}^{2}z{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
